summary: The agent implemented nearly all seedable-lazy behavior and preserved all baseline functionality, but 2 of 13 new tests failed because hybrid with-methods always allocate instead of returning the same instance when an identical explicit seed is already present.
quick_failure_summary: Repeated with-method calls using the same explicit seed return a new equal object instead of the original instance.

details.reasoning: The custom seedable-lazy wither generation unconditionally constructs and seeds a copy. It correctly avoids treating a merely computed fallback as an existing explicit seed, but it never checks whether the attribute is already explicitly seeded with an equal value. Consequently, both a repeated scalar seed and a repeated OptionalInt.empty() seed violate the established generated-wither identity contract.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added substantial focused coverage, but its tests checked that an equal computed fallback creates a distinct explicitly seeded value without also checking the complementary case that repeating the same already-explicit seed returns this.

justification.issue_description: Seedable-lazy with-methods must return the current immutable instance when the attribute is already explicitly seeded and the requested seed is equal, while still creating a new explicitly seeded instance when equality is only with a computed fallback.
justification.evidence: The prompt says the capability is exposed through generated with-methods and specifically distinguishes equality with a computed fallback, which implies seed-origin-aware equality handling. Existing Immutables.generator wither templates repeatedly use equality checks followed by `return this`, and visible tests such as value-fixture/test/org/immutables/fixture/with/WithEnumsTest.java and value-fixture/test/org/immutables/fixture/ValuesTest.java assert same-instance behavior for unchanged withers. The agent's generated methods instead always create a copy and call the seed helper.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented requirement or test mismatch. Although the exact repeated-explicit-seed optimization is not stated verbatim, it is a longstanding, readily visible contract of generated with-methods in both the generator and existing tests. A competent implementation should preserve that contract while using explicit-seed state to avoid incorrectly returning this for a merely computed fallback.

problem_assessment.notes: The task spans processor metadata, immutable and modifiable code generation, copying, serialization, diagnostics, null/falsey/container cases, and seed-origin tracking. The two failing identity assertions are deterministic and align with established repository behavior. The exact identity optimization could have been stated more explicitly, but it was reasonably inferable from the visible codebase and tests.

evidence: JUnit XML reports 326 of 326 baseline tests passing and 11 of 13 new tests passing; the two failures are ordinary AssertionErrors after generated code execution, not setup or bootstrap failures.
The verifier completed compilation and test execution successfully enough to isolate both failures to same-instance assertions in SeedableLazy_6c7a1b_Test.
The trajectory shows the agent ran focused and broad Maven validation successfully on its own tests before finishing.
The only notable tool limitation was `/bin/sh: rg: not found`; the agent immediately used grep instead, so this did not materially divert or block the work.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful environment or verifier blocker was found; the hidden failures are explained by a localized implementation omission in seedable-lazy withers.
